Retrieved on 3 October 2021. | years_active = 2012–present (MMA) | mma_ko_win = 28 | mma_sub_win = 3 | mma_dec_win = 1 | mma_ko_loss = 5 | mma_sub_loss = 1 | mma_dec_loss = | mma_draw = 1 | mma_nc = | website = {{URL|www.jiribjp.com}} | sherdog = 97529 | footnotes = | updated = | Kickboxing record = | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[Muay Thai]]}} {{MedalCompetition|{{flagicon|CZE}}}} [[:cs:Česká Muaythai Asociace|Czech National Championships]] {{MedalGold|2011 [[Prague]] |−86 kg}} | module = {{infobox social media personality | child = yes | youtube_handle = JiriProchazkaBJP | youtube_display_name = Jiri BJP Prochazka | youtube_years_active = | youtube_genre = | youtube_subscribers = 75 thousand | youtube_views = 6 million | stats_update = January 17, 2026 }} }} '''Jiří Procházka''' ({{IPA|cs|ˈjɪr̝iː ˈproxaːska|lang|Jiří Procházka.ogg}}; {{IPA|cs|ˈjɪrka||Cs-Jirka.oga}}; born October 14, 1992) is a Czech professional [[mixed martial artist]]. He currently competes in the [[Light heavyweight (MMA)|Light Heavyweight]] division of the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship]] (UFC), where he is a former [[UFC Light Heavyweight Champion]] and the first Czech fighter to win a UFC championship. He was the inaugural [[Rizin Fighting Federation#Light Heavyweight Championship|Rizin Fighting Federation Light Heavyweight Champion]] and the inaugural Gladiator Fighting Championship Light Heavyweight Champion. As of April 14, 2026, he is #3 in the [[Meta Platforms|Meta]] [[UFC rankings#Light Heavyweight|UFC light heavyweight rankings]].{{Cite web |title=UFC Rankings, Division Rankings, P4P rankings, UFC Champions {{!}} UFC.com |url=https://www.ufc.com/rankings |access-date=2026-04-14|website=www.ufc.com}} ==Early life== Procházka was born on October 14, 1992, in a hospital in [[Znojmo]] in [[Czechoslovakia]] (now the [[Czech Republic]]), but he comes from the nearby village of [[Hostěradice]].{{cite web |title=Podávala se snídaně a šlo se fandit. Procházka ve svém rodišti zažehl euforii|url=https://www.idnes.cz/sport/mma/jiri-prochazka-mma-titul-ufc-fanousci-hosteradice.A220612_215334_sport-mma_ald|website=[[Mladá fronta Dnes]]|publisher=[[Mafra (company)|Mafra]]|language=cs|date=2022-06-13|access-date=2023-11-09}} Procházka's father died at age 27 when Jiří was six years old.{{Cite web|title=Jiří Procházka {{!}} Český zápasník podmanil Japonsko, teď míří do Ameriky|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dDxDcln2Foc|website=YouTube|date=13 December 2019|access-date=11 July 2020|language=cs}}{{Cite web |title=Jiří Procházka:Kingdom of Heaven {{!}} Stories {{!}} Bez frází |url=https://www.bezfrazi.cz/stories/jiri-prochazka/kingdom-of-heaven |access-date=21 December 2025 |website=www.bezfrazi.cz |language=en}} In his youth, Procházka played amateur [[association football|football]] for TJ Družstevník Hostěradice. He was also an active [[freestyle BMX]] rider and a [[floorball]] player.{{cite news |last=Budný|first=Lubomír|title=Na vtipkování není při zápasech čas, říká bojovník Jiří Procházka|url=https://znojemsky.denik.cz/ostatni_region/na-vtipkovani-neni-pri-zapasech-cas-rika-bojovnik-jiri-prochazka-20191031.html|newspaper=[[Znojemský Deník|Deník]]|publisher=Vltave Labe Media|language=cs|date=2019-10-31|access-date=2023-11-09}} As a teen, Procházka partook in street fights almost weekly, getting into more than 100 of them. This eventually led him to join the [[Hooligan firms|hooligan firm]] tied to Procházka's local football team, [[FC Zbrojovka Brno]], where he would take part in organized group street fights with clubs of other teams, even participating in 30-on-30 brawls.{{Cite web |last=Raimondi |first=Marc |date=2022-06-08 |title=Inside Jiri Prochazka's warrior path from soccer hooligan to UFC title contender |url=https://www.espn.com/mma/story/_/id/34052661/inside-jiri-prochazka-warrior-path-soccer-hooligan-ufc-title-contender|website=[[ESPN]]|access-date=2022-06-09}} Procházka first encountered mixed martial arts before beginning high school, after a friend showed him videos of kickboxer [[Ramon Dekkers]] and mixed martial artists [[Mirko Cro Cop|Mirko Filipovic]] and [[Fedor Emelianenko]].{{Cite web|title=UFC 275's Jiri Prochazka talks patient rise to championship opportunity |url=https://nypost.com/2022/06/01/jiri-prochazka-talks-patient-rise-to-ufc-275-title-shot/|website=[[New York Post]]|date=1 June 2022|access-date=3 June 2022}} After watching the film [[Never Back Down]], he began to train in martial arts, in particular [[Muay Thai|Thai boxing]]. ==Mixed martial arts career== ===Gladiator Fighting Championship=== ====Debut and initial fights==== Procházka made his professional MMA debut in April 2012 for the Gladiator Fighting Championship, the biggest promotion in his native Czech Republic at the time. He amassed a 7–2 record within his first two years of fighting professionally. ====Inaugural Light Heavyweight Champion==== In his tenth professional bout, he won the inaugural GCF Light Heavyweight Championship in the back-and-forth fight against Czech MMA pioneer Martin Šolc via flying knee knockout on December 7, 2013, at GCF 26 FN. Video of the bout went viral in the Czech Republic and Procházka was also awarded a post-fight bonus.[https://sport.aktualne.cz/ostatni-sporty/video-svatek-mma-do-klece-se-vraci-brutalni-prochazka/r~09732da0b02511e39d8a0025900fea04/ VIDEO Svátek MMA: Do klece se vrací brutální Procházka!], ''Aktuálně'' 2014/03/21. Retrieved on 12 July 2020. The fight was later awarded 'Czech Fight of the Year' by major media outlets.[https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/ostatni-dalsi-sporty/198383/loni-dal-ko-roku-nyni-ma-gladiator-mma-prochazka-v-planu-znicit-nemce.html Loni dal KO roku. Nyní má gladiátor MMA Procházka v plánu zničit Němce], ''[[Blesk|iSport.cz]]'' 2014. Retrieved on 9 January 2021. Procházka defended his title against Tomáš Penz on June 6, 2014, at GCF 28: Cage Fight 4. He won the fight via technical knockout due to a flying knee in 41 seconds.[http://fighternews.cz/mma-v-brne-slavili-prochazka-a-kuznik/ MMA: V Brně slavili Procházka a Kuzník] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220419150025/http://fighternews.cz/mma-v-brne-slavili-prochazka-a-kuznik/ |date=2022-04-19 }}, ''FighterNews.cz'' 15 June 2014. Retrieved on 10 January 2021. Procházka signed a deal with the [[Rizin Fighting Federation]] shortly before his win against Evgeni Kondratov. After amassing a record of 14–2–1 during his first three years in the sport, Procházka as the first Czech entered the [[Rizin Fighting Federation]] in 2015.[https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/ostatni-mma/256106/cesky-mma-bojovnik-radi-v-japonsku-prochazka-knockoutoval-soupere.html Český MMA bojovník řádí v Japonsku. Procházka knockoutoval soupeře], ''[[Blesk|iSport.cz]]'' 2015/12/29. Retrieved on 2 September 2020.[http://www.rizinff.com/en/interview/20151221_3332.html The Fight that was my turning point. Satoshi Ishii / Jiri Prochazka], ''Rizin FF'' 2015/12/21. Retrieved on 2 September 2020. ===Rizin Fighting Federation=== ====Heavyweight Grand Prix==== Procházka made his promotional debut against [[Satoshi Ishii]] on December 29, 2015, in the World Grand Prix 2015 –100 kg tournament at the Rizin FF's first event Saraba no Utake. He won the quarter-final fight via knockout in the first round.[https://www.mmafighting.com/2015/12/29/10676940/rizin-results-aoki-vs-sakuraba Rizin Results: Aoki vs. Sakuraba], ''MMA Fighting'' 2015/12/29. Retrieved on 2 September 2020. Procházka's next fight in the Rizin FF's -100 kg tournament was at Iza no Mai on December 31, 2015. He won the semi-final fight against [[Vadim Nemkov]] via technical knockout. Later that same night, he lost in the final round against [[Muhammed Lawal]] via knockout in the first round.[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2603949-rizin-ff-2-highlights-results-and-top-knockouts-from-thursdays-fights Rizin FF 2: Highlights, Results and Top Knockouts from Thursday's Fights], ''Bleacher Report'' 2015/12/31. Retrieved on 2 September 2020. Procházka weighed in at 95.9 kgs (211.5 pounds) for the tournament.[https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/bouts/235527-rizin-fighting-world-grand-prix-2015-ji-denisa-prochzka-vs-satoshi-ishii Satoshi Ishii vs. Jiří Procházka], ''Tapology'' 2015/12/29. Retrieved on 14 April 2021. Procházka faced [[Kazuyuki Fujita]] on April 17, 2016, at Rizin 1 at a catchweight of 110 kgs (242.5 pounds). Procházka weighed in at 98.6 kgs (217.3 pounds) for the bout.[https://www.bloodyelbow.com/2016/4/16/11443648/rizin-1-prochazka-vs-fujita-weigh-in-results Rizin 1: Prochazka vs. Fujita weigh-in results], ''BloodyElbow.com'' 2016/04/16. Retrieved on 14 April 2021. He won the fight via technical knockout in the first round.[https://www.mmafighting.com/2016/4/17/11446110/rizin-1-results-fujita-vs-prochazka Rizin 1 Results: Fujita vs. Prochazka], ''MMA Fighting'' 2016/04/17. Retrieved on 2 September 2020. Procházka faced Mark Tanios on September 25, 2016, at Rizin 2 - Rizin Fighting World Grand Prix 2016: Opening Round. He won the fight via unanimous decision.[https://profiboxing.cz/mma/aktuality/videofoto-samuraj-prochazka-vyhral-i-na-jedne-noze-bavil-i-sileny-kun VIDEO+FOTO Samuraj Procházka vyhrál i na jedné noze, bavil také 'Šílený kůň'] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220426033851/https://profiboxing.cz/mma/aktuality/videofoto-samuraj-prochazka-vyhral-i-na-jedne-noze-bavil-i-sileny-kun |date=2022-04-26 }}, ''ProfiBoxing.cz'' 2016/09/26. Retrieved on 2 September 2020. Procházka suffered a knee injury during the fight and was subsequently pulled from the tournament.[https://mmasucka.com/2018/05/29/asakura-vs-rena-ii-jiri-prochazka-among-three-additions-to-rizin-11/ Asakura vs. RENA II, Jiri Prochazka among three additions to RIZIN 11], ''MMA Sucka'' 2016/05/29. Retrieved on 10 January 2021. ====Return to Light Heavyweight==== Procházka faced Willian Roberto Alves on September 29, 2017, at Fusion FN 16 - Cage Fight, the homecoming event organized by his team. He won the fight via technical knockout in the first round.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z10VdlK9iWM 8. Jiří „Denisa“ Procházka vs Wilian Roberto „Cowboy“ Alves], ''FUSION FIGHT NIGHT'' 2017/10/07. Retrieved on 12 July 2020. Procházka faced [[Karl Albrektsson]] on December 29, 2017, at Rizin Fighting World Grand Prix 2017 - Bantamweight Tournament: 2nd Round. He won the fight via technical knockout in the first round.[https://sport.tn.nova.cz/clanek/ufc-je-blizko-cesky-bijec-denisa-nadelil-svedovi-krvavy-knock-out.html UFC je blízko! Český bijec Denisa nadělil Švédovi krvavý knock-out!] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190227031104/http://sport.tn.nova.cz/clanek/ufc-je-blizko-cesky-bijec-denisa-nadelil-svedovi-krvavy-knock-out.html |date=2019-02-27 }}, ''[[TV Nova (Czech TV channel)|TV Nova]]'' 2017/12/29. Retrieved on 2 September 2020. Procházka faced [[Bruno Cappelozza]] on July 28, 2018, at Rizin 11. He won the fight via knockout in the first round.[https://www.mmafighting.com/2018/7/29/17626890/takanori-gomi-knocks-out-melvin-guillard-rizin-11 Takanori Gomi knocks out Melvin Guillard at Rizin 11], ''MMA Fighting'' 2018/07/29. Retrieved on 12 July 2020. Procházka faced Jake Heun on September 30, 2018, at Rizin 13. He won the fight via technical knockout in the first round.[https://www.sport.cz/ostatni/bojove-sporty/clanek/1027563-tajfun-uderil-pote-prochazka-v-japonsku-ukoncil-americana.html Tajfun udeřil. Poté Procházka v Japonsku ukončil Američana], ''Sport.cz'' 2018/10/02. Retrieved on 12 July 2020. Procházka was scheduled to face [[Emanuel Newton]] on December 31, 2018, at Rizin 14.[https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/bouts/398878-rizin-14-jiri-denisa-prochazka-vs-emanuel-the-hardcore-kid-newton CANCELLED MMA BOUT Jiří Procházka vs. Emanuel Newton], ''Tapology'' 2020/12/18. Retrieved on 28 April 2021. However, Newton was pulled out of the fight, citing a rib injury. Procházka remained on the card and was rescheduled to face [[Brandon Halsey]].[https://mmasucka.com/2018/12/18/brandon-halsey-replaces-newton-vs-jiri-prochazka-at-rizin-14/ Brandon Halsey replaces Newton vs. Jiri Prochazka at RIZIN 14], ''MMA Sucka'' 2020/12/18. Retrieved on 28 April 2021. He won the fight via technical knockout in the first round.[https://www.sherdog.com/news/articles/By-The-Numbers-Volkan-Oezdemir-vs-Jiri-Prochazka-173880 BY THE NUMBERS: VOLKAN OEZDEMIR VS. JIRI PROCHAZKA], ''Sherdog'' 2020/07/10. Retrieved on 12 July 2020. ====Inaugural Light Heavyweight Champion==== Procházka faced [[Muhammed Lawal]] in rematch on April 21, 2019, at Rizin 15 for the inaugural Rizin FF Light Heavyweight Championship. He won the fight via technical knockout in the third round.{{cite web |last1=Cruz |first1=Guilherme |title=Takanori Gomi knocks out Melvin Guillard at Rizin 11 |url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2018/7/29/17626890/takanori-gomi-knocks-out-melvin-guillard-rizin-11 |website=MMA Fighting |date=29 July 2018 |publisher=Vox Media LLC |accessdate=17 September 2020}} Procházka faced [[Fábio Maldonado]] on October 12, 2019, at Rizin 19: Lightweight Grand Prix 1st Round at a catchweight of 100 kgs (220.4 pounds). Procházka weighed in at 97.90 kgs (215.8 pounds) for the bout.[https://www.sherdog.com/news/news/RIZIN-19-Weighin-Results-Everyone-Makes-Weight-163477 RIZIN 19 WEIGH-IN RESULTS: EVERYONE MAKES WEIGHT], ''Sherdog'' 2019/10/11. Retrieved on 14 April 2021. He won the fight via knockout in the first round.[https://www.mmafighting.com/2019/10/12/20910934/rizin-19-jiri-prochazka-blasts-fabio-maldonado-kai-asakura-ulka-sasaki-mma Rizin 19 results: Jiri Prochazka blasts through Fabio Maldonado, Kai Asakura overwhelms Ulka Sasaki], ''MMA Fighting'' 2019/10/12. Retrieved on 12 July 2020. Procházka defended his title against [[C. B. Dollaway]] on December 31, 2019, at Rizin 20.{{cite web|url=https://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Jiri-ProchazkaCB-Dollaway-Kai-AsakuraManel-Kape-Title-Bouts-Set-for-Rizin-20-167089|title=Jiri Prochazka-C.B. Dollaway, Kai Asakura-Manel Kape Title Bouts Set for Rizin 20|date=December 4, 2019|work=[[Sherdog]]|author=Tristen Critchfield}} He won the fight via knockout in the first round.[https://www.mmamania.com/2019/12/31/21044276/video-jiri-prochazka-dribbles-cb-dollaway-one-punch-knockout-rizin-20-mma Video: Jiri Prochazka dribbles CB Dollaway with one-punch knockout at RIZIN 20], ''MMA Mania'' 2019/12/31. Retrieved on 12 July 2020. This was the last fight on the Procházka's contract with Rizin. After the fight, he signed a new deal with the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] and vacated his title. ===Ultimate Fighting Championship=== ====Debut and contender fight==== Procházka signed a contract with the [[UFC]] in January 2020.[https://www.ufc.com/news/business-usual-jiri-prochazka-ufc-251-fight-island BUSINESS AS USUAL FOR JIRI PROCHAZKA], ''[[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]]'' 2020/07/07. Retrieved on 2 September 2020. He made his promotional debut against former [[UFC Light Heavyweight Champion|UFC Light Heavyweight title]] challenger [[Volkan Oezdemir]] on July 11, 2020, at [[UFC 251]].{{cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/volkan-oezdemir-jiri-prochazka-headline-ufc-251-prelims-on-tsn-1.1494391|title=Oezdemir, Prochazka headline UFC 251 Prelims on TSN|date=July 11, 2020|work=[[The Sports Network]]|author=Ken Rodney}} He won via knockout in the second round and was awarded a ''[[List of UFC bonus award recipients|Performance of the Night]]'' bonus award. With this win, he's the only man to give Oezdemir a KO loss in his MMA career.{{Cite web |date=2020-07-12 |title=UFC 251 bonuses: Rose Namajunas-Jessica Andrade war nets 'Fight of the Night' honors |url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2020/07/ufc-251-bonuses-rose-namajunas-jessica-andrade-war-nets-fight-of-the-night-honors |access-date=2022-03-21 |website=MMA Junkie |language=en-US}} Procházka was expected to face two–time [[UFC Light Heavyweight Championship]] title challenger [[Dominick Reyes]] on February 27, 2021, at [[UFC Fight Night 186]].{{cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2020/10/28/21537780/dominick-reyes-vs-jiri-prochazka-expected-to-headline-ufc-event-on-feb-27|title=Dominick Reyes vs. Jiri Prochazka expected to headline UFC event on Feb. 27|date=October 28, 2020|publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Damon Martin}} However, in late January, Reyes was pulled from the fight, due to injury, and the bout was rescheduled for May 1, 2021, at [[UFC on ESPN: Reyes vs. Procházka]].{{Cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2021/01/ufc-news-jairzinho-rozenstruik-ciryl-gane-new-main-event-feb-27|title=Reyes vs. Prochazka out, Rozenstruik vs. Gane in as UFC Fight Night headliner for Feb. 27|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Alexander Mookie|date=2021-01-30|access-date=2021-01-30}}{{cite web|url=https://www.mmamania.com/2021/2/11/22278838/dominick-reyes-vs-jiri-prochazka-rebooked-ufc-fight-night-main-event-on-may-1|title=Dominick Reyes vs Jiri Prochazka rebooked for UFC Fight Night main event on May 1|date=February 11, 2021|publisher=mmamania.com|author=Jesse Holland}} In a back and forth fight, Procházka won the fight via knockout in the second round.{{Cite web|last=Doherty|first=Dan|date=2021-05-02|title=UFC Vegas 25 Results: Jiri Prochazka Lands Stunning Elbow to KO Dominick Reyes|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2021/05/02/ufc-vegas-25-results-jiri-prochazka/|access-date=2021-05-02|website=Cageside Press|language=en-US}} With this win, he was awarded the ''[[List of UFC bonus award recipients|Performance of the Night]]'' and ''[[List of UFC bonus award recipients|Fight of the Night]]'' bonus awards.{{cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/lists/ufc-espn-23-bonuses-jiri-prochazka-double-100000-giga-chikadze|title=UFC on ESPN 23 bonuses: Jiri Prochazka double-dips for $100,000|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Staff|date=2021-05-02|access-date=2021-05-02}} ====UFC Light Heavyweight Champion==== [[File:JiriProchazkaBelt2022.png|thumb|right|Procházka (left) with his [[List of UFC champions#Light Heavyweight Championship|UFC Light Heavyweight belt]] during a Czech [[talk show]] in 2022]] Procházka was scheduled to face [[Glover Teixeira]] for the [[UFC Light Heavyweight Championship]] on May 7, 2022, at [[UFC 274]].{{Cite web|title=UFC 274 fight card: Glover Teixeira set to defend light heavyweight title against Jiri Prochazka in May|url=https://www.cbssports.com/mma/news/ufc-274-fight-card-glover-teixeira-set-to-defend-light-heavyweight-title-against-jiri-prochazka-in-may/|access-date=2022-01-23|website=CBSSports.com|date=22 January 2022 |language=en}} However, the bout was postponed to June 11, 2022, at [[UFC 275]] for undisclosed reasons.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2022/2/27/22953018/glover-teixeira-vs-jiri-prochazka-championship-fight-at-ufc-274-rescheduled-for-ufc-275|title= Glover Teixeira vs. Jiri Prochazka championship fight at UFC 274 rescheduled for UFC 275|work=mmafighting.com|author=Alexander K. Lee|date=2022-02-27|access-date=2022-02-27}} In a back-and-forth fight which saw both fighters get dropped multiple times, Procházka won the bout and title via rear-naked choke submission in the fifth round, becoming the first Czech fighter to win a UFC championship.{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Jay |date=2022-06-12 |title=UFC 275: Jiri Prochazka Secures Late Submission, Dethrones Glover unorthodox and unpredictable fighting style, blending traditional martial arts philosophy with an aggressive, high-risk approach. Fighting out of a wide stance with his hands often down, he relies heavily on head movement, timing, and reflexes rather than textbook defense.{{cite web |last=Marrocco |first=Steven |title=Jiří Procházka's chaos is a system — and it's working |url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2022/6/9/23157092/ufc-jiri-prochazka-style-analysis |website=MMAFighting |date=June 9, 2022 |access-date=June 28, 2025}} Rather than focus on control or efficiency, Procházka embraces a philosophy of total engagement, frequently taking damage to create openings for counterattacks. He has stated in interviews that he prefers a mindset of "[[no-mind]]" in the cage—drawing from [[Zen]] and [[Bushido]] principles to fight instinctively rather than strategically.{{cite web |last=Wagenheim |first=Jeff |title=Jiří Procházka says he doesn't fight opponents — he fights the moment |url=https://www.espn.com/mma/story/_/id/34045329/ufc-jiri-prochazka-mindset-fight-style-philosophy |website=ESPN |date=June 8, 2022 |access-date=June 28, 2025}} Defensively, Procházka has drawn criticism for leaving openings, but his durability, recovery, and offensive unpredictability have allowed him to survive and turn the tide in chaotic exchanges.{{cite web |last=Sherdog Staff |title=Scouting Report: Jiří Procházka |url=https://www.sherdog.com/news/articles/Scouting-Report-Jiri-Prochazka-188002 |website=Sherdog |date=June 6, 2022 |access-date=June 28, 2025}} ==Personal life== Procházka is well known as a devoted follower of the [[Bushido|Bushido principles]], the [[Samurai#Philosophy|samurai moral values]] and [[Miyamoto Musashi]]'s teachings and philosophy, especially [[The Book of Five Rings|Musashi's ''The Book of Five Rings'']], which Procházka considers a life-changing book for him.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QFEpKD122ZU K.O. magazín (41) - Jiří "Denisa" Procházka], ''SPORT 5'' 2019/10/30. Retrieved on 11 July 2020. He is a supporter of [[FC Zbrojovka Brno]] and was involved in organized [[football hooliganism]], including pre-arranged fights, until he started his professional combat sports career.[https://www.fczbrno.cz/clanek.asp?id=6052 Jiří "Denisa" Procházka na Zbrojovce!], ''[[FC Zbrojovka Brno]]''. Retrieved on 12 January 2021. Besides his native Czech, Procházka is conversational in English and has actively improved his proficiency in the language since joining the promotion.[https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/ostatni-mma-ufc/381035/prochazka-leti-na-ufc-ostrov-vyladil-uces-i-anglictinu-koho-vital-se-zbrani.html Procházka letí na UFC ostrov. '''Santiago Luna Velazco''' (born 6 August 2004) is an American-born Mexican professional [[mixed martial artist]] who currently competes in the [[Bantamweight (MMA)|Bantamweight]] division of the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship]] (UFC).<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ortiz|first=Alexander|url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/deportes/2025/09/20/santiago-luna-la-promesa-mexicana-que-debuto-en-ufc-con-nocaut-en-el-primer-round/|title=Santiago Luna: la promesa mexicana que debutó en UFC con nocaut en el primer round|date=2025-09-14|access-date=2025-10-23|website=Infobae}}</ref>

==Early life==
Luna was born in [[San Diego]], California, and raised in [[Tijuana, Baja California]], Mexico.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/ufc/article/ufc-undercard-overview-bryce-mitchell-facing-super-prospect-luna/|title=UFC undercard overview: Bryce Mitchell facing super prospect Luna|website=Sportsnet|first=Mike|last=Johnston|date=June 4, 2026|access-date=June 6, 2026}}</ref> Before embarking on MMA, he had a career in [[Greco-Roman wrestling]], where he was a three-time national champion and qualified for the [[Pan American Games]]. He began training at [[Entram Gym]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bitter|first=Shawn|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2025/09/13/welcome-to-the-ufc-santiago-luna/|title=Welcome to the UFC: Santiago Luna|date=2025-09-13|access-date=2026-04-23|website=Cageside Press}}</ref>

==Mixed martial arts career==
===Ultimate Warrior Challenge Mexico===
Luna made his professional debut for the [[Ultimate Warrior Challenge Mexico]] on April 28, 2023, at [[UWC Mexico 43]], where he secured a victory over Einar González with a rear-naked choke in the first round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/bouts/757207-uwc-43-santiago-borderboy-luna-vs-einar-karel-gonzalez|title=Santiago Luna vs. Einar González, UWC 43 {{!}} MMA Bout|access-date=2026-04-23|website=Tapology}}</ref>

Later that same year, he won his next two fights against Luis Gerardo Aguillón at [[UWC Mexico 46]], and then against Emilio Galindo at [[UWC Mexico 49]] on October 27; in both, he applied the same submission hold.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/bouts/778863-uwc-46-santiago-borderboy-luna-vs-gerardo-aguillon|title=Santiago Luna vs. Luis Gerardo Aguilón, UWC 46 {{!}} MMA Bout|access-date=2026-04-23|website=Tapology}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/bouts/806546-uwc-49-santiago-borderboy-luna-vs-emilio-jaguar-galindo|title=Santiago Luna vs. Emilio Galindo, UWC 49 {{!}} MMA Bout|access-date=2026-04-23|website=Tapology}}</ref>

On April 7, 2024, Luna faced Josimar Cuevas at [[UWC Mexico 52]]. He won the fight by technical knockout in the first round.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Beaupre|first=Drew|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/mma/news/ufc-21-year-old-fighter-two-weeks-notice-noche-ufc-santiago-luna|title=UFC calls in 21-year-old fighter on less than two weeks' notice for Noche UFC debut|date=2025-09-03|access-date=2026-04-23|website=si.com}}</ref>

===Ultimate Fighting Championship===
With a 6–0 record and a 100% finish rate, Luna made his [[Ultimate Fighting Championship]] (UFC) debut, replacing fellow countryman [[David Martínez (fighter)|David Martínez]] as Quang Le's opponent for [[UFC Fight Night: Lopes vs. Silva|UFC Fight Night 259]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://lado.mx/noticia/19142663|title=Santiago Luna vs. Quang Le ¿A qué hora y dónde ver EN VIVO el debut del tijuanense ‘Border Boy’ en la Noche UFC 2025 del 13 de septiembre?|date=2025-09-13|access-date=2026-04-23|website=Lado.mx}}</ref> Luna won the fight via first-round knockout.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Díaz Valdivia|first=Mauricio|url=https://www.record.com.mx/extremo/el-mexicano-santiago-luna-gana-por-nocaut-en-su-debut-en-ufc-y-lanza-emotivo-mensaje|title=El mexicano Santiago Luna gana por nocaut en su debut en UFC y lanza emotivo mensaje|date=2025-09-13|access-date=2026-04-23|website=Récord}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=2026-04-23 |date=2025-09-13 |first=Patrizio |last=Cano |title=Tijuanense Santiago Luna debuta en la Noche UFC con nocaut en el primer round |url=https://www.elimparcial.com/deporte/2025/09/13/tijuanense-santiago-luna-debuta-en-la-noche-ufc-con-nocaut-en-el-primer-round/ |website=El Imparcial}}<!-- auto-translated from unknown (Italian or Spanish) by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> His performance in the octagon earned him his first ''[[List of UFC bonus award recipients|Performance of the Night]]'' bonus.<ref name="nocheufc3">{{Cite web|last=Taylor|first=Chris|url=https://www.bjpenn.com/mma-news/noche-ufc/noche-ufc-3-bonus-report-diego-lopes-takes-home-two-bonuses/|title=Noche UFC 3 Bonus Report: Diego Lopes takes home two bonuses|date=2025-09-13|access-date=2026-04-23|website=bjpenn.com}}</ref>

Luna faced Angel Pacheco on February 28, 2026, at [[UFC Fight Night: Moreno vs. Kavanagh|UFC Fight Night 268]]. He won the fight by unanimous decision.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Holt|first=Nick|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2026/02/28/ufc-mexico-city-promising-santiago-luna-shines-against-angel-pacheco/|title=UFC Mexico City: Promising Santiago Luna Shines Against Angel Pacheco|date=2026-02-28|access-date=2026-04-23|website=Cageside Press}}</ref>

Replacing [[Victor Henry (fighter)|Victor Henry]], Luna faced [[Bryce Mitchell]] on June 6, 2026, at [[UFC Fight Night 278]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://heavy.com/sports/ufc/mitchell-new-opponent-ufc-vegas-118/|title=Bryce Mitchell gets new undefeated opponent for UFC Vegas 118|publisher=heavy.com|author=Marcel Dorff|date=2026-05-28|access-date=2026-05-28}}</ref> He lost the fight via an arm-triangle submission in the third round.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2026/06/06/ufc-vegas-118-bryce-mitchell-locks-up-late-sub-on-santiago-luna/|title=UFC Vegas 118: Bryce Mitchell locks up late sub on Santiago Luna|publisher=cagesidepress.com|author=Nick Holt|date=2026-06-06|access-date=2026-06-07}}</ref>

Luna is scheduled to face [[Aleksandre Topuria]] on November 21, 2026, at [[UFC Fight Night 294]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/polideportivo/aleksandre-topuria-ya-tiene-rival-santiago-luna-f202609-n/|title=Aleksandre Topuria ya tiene rival: Santiago Luna|publisher=as.com|author=Diario AS|date=2026-09-16|access-date=2026-09-17}} {{in lang|es}}</ref>

As of October 24, 2026, he is #7 in the [[Meta Platforms|Meta]] [[UFC rankings#Light Heavyweight|UFC light heavyweight rankings]].{{Cite web |title=UFC Rankings, Division Rankings, P4P rankings, UFC Champions {{!}} UFC.com |url=https://www.ufc.com/rankings |access-date=2026-10-24|website=www.ufc.com}} ==Early life and kickboxing career== Stirling was born on 7 November 1997, in [[Upper Hutt]], New Zealand.{{cite web|url=https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/fighters/259609-navajo-sterling|title=Navajo Stirling|publisher=Tapology|access-date=June 15, 2026}} He attended [[Upper Hutt College]] and played rugby growing up, but grew tired of the necessity to rely on teammates and signed up for [[karate]] classes at a nearby gym.{{cite news|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/sport/439408/king-in-the-ring-chases-passport-to-fight-island|title=King in the Ring chases passport to Fight Island|work=[[Radio New Zealand]]|first=Finlay|last=Dunseath|date=29 March 2021|access-date=June 17, 2026}} Years later, Stirling developed an interest in [[mixed martial arts]] (MMA), specifically by watching [[Conor McGregor]], and started dreaming of fighting in the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship]] (UFC).{{cite news|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/350498329/king-in-the-ring-great-navajo-stirling-on-track-to-achieve-ufc-dream-after-move-to-city-kickboxing|title=King in the Ring great Navajo Stirling on track to achieve UFC dream after move to City Kickboxing|work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]|first=Stephen|last=Foote|date=September 7, 2022|access-date=June 17, 2026}} In 2020, while visiting his brother in [[Auckland]], he tagged along on a trip to the [[City Kickboxing]] gym, where he realised that kickboxing could be his chance to follow his UFC dreams. Stirling later stated: "That visit made me realise I should have been here ages ago." After returning home, he began training under Sone Vannathy at the Arch Angels Thai Kickboxing Gym in [[Wellington]]. Stirling fought at the amateur level before moving to The Lion Pit, also in Wellington, where he began his professional career. He won the [[King in the Ring#King in the Ring 92III|King in the Ring 92 kg III]] tournament in December 2020 as "a largely unknown prospect" by defeating Nato La'auli in the final.{{cite news|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/combat-sports/125476956/king-in-the-ring-navajo-stirling-wants-second-title-then-follow-city-kickboxing-blueprint-toward-ufc|title=King in the Ring: Navajo Stirling wants second title then follow City Kickboxing blueprint toward UFC|first=Mat|last=Kermeen|work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]|date=June 17, 2021|access-date=June 17, 2026}} Stirling compiled a 6–1 professional record before moving to [[City Kickboxing]] in [[Auckland]] in March 2021. That June, he won the [[King in the Ring#King in the Ring 100IV|King in the Ring 100 kg IV]] tournament by defeating James Craughwell in the final,{{cite news|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/combat-sports/125509200/king-in-the-ring-kickboxing-referee-wears-punch-to-the-face-during-fight-navajo-stirlings-rise-continues|title=King in the Ring: Kick-boxing referee wears punch to the face during fight, Navajo Stirling's rise continues|work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]|date=June 20, 2021|access-date=June 17, 2026}} joining [[Israel Adesanya]] and [[Carlos Ulberg]] as the only two-weight champions in the history of the tournament.{{cite news|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/sport/445053/stirling-striving-to-be-crowned-two-time-king|title=Stirling striving to be crowned two-time King|work=[[Radio New Zealand]]|date=June 18, 2021|access-date=June 17, 2026}} On 9 September 2022, Stirling was scheduled to face Jesse Astill in the co-main event of the [[King in the Ring#King in the Ring SUPERV|King in the Ring SUPERV]] event for the WKBF Professional Heavyweight K1 Championship.{{cite news|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/combat-sports/300681607/its-going-to-happen-king-in-the-ring-champion-navajo-stirlings-goal-to-become-a-ufc-superstar|title='It's going to happen': King in the Ring champion Navajo Stirling's goal to become a UFC superstar|work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]|first=Sam|last=Wilson|date=September 8, 2022|access-date=June 17, 2026}} ==Mixed martial arts career== During his kickboxing career, Stirling also developed his [[grappling]] and [[jiu-jitsu]] skills in preparation for a switch to MMA, even competing at regional [[no-gi]] competitions. He made his professional MMA debut on 23 September 2022, defeating James Craughwell via [[unanimous decision]] at Shuriken Fight Series 12 in [[Auckland]] to capture the Shuriken [[Heavyweight (MMA)|heavyweight]] championship. However, Stirling struggled to find willing opponents at the regional scene and waited over a year for his first title defence, during which he continued rounding out his skills.{{cite news|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/ufc/ufc-city-kickboxing-prospect-grapples-with-improved-technique-for-step-up-to-big-time/BBCNHLNV6JHRBIRHQ6BLHRIFZ4/|title=UFC: City Kickboxing prospect grapples with improved technique for step up to big time|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|first=Callum|last=Tasker|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=June 17, 2026}} He retained the title by defeating Kelvin Fitial via first-round [[technical knockout]] (TKO) at Shuriken Fight Series 16. On 4 May 2024, Stirling stopped Stu Dare in the first round of their fight at Hex Fight Series 30.{{cite news|url=https://www.teaonews.co.nz/2024/05/06/one-step-closer-to-ufc-for-navajo-stirling/|title=One step closer to UFC for Navajo Stirling|work=[[Te Ao Māori News]]|first=Mare|last=Haimona-Riki|date=May 5, 2024|access-date=June 17, 2026}} The following month, he defeated Sam Kei via third-round TKO at Hex Fight Series 31 to capture the vacant Hex [[Light heavyweight (MMA)|light heavyweight]] championship.{{cite news|url=https://www.fightnewsaustralia.com/navajo-stirling-gets-call-up-to-dana-whites-contender-series/|title=Navajo Stirling gets call up to Dana White's Contender Series|work=Fight News Australia|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 17, 2026}} On 10 September 2024, Stirling [[knockout|knocked out]] Phillip Latu in the second round of their fight in the main event of [[Dana White's Contender Series season 8|Dana White's Contender Series 71]].
